question: Public procurement represents a major share of public expenditure across the EU. However, procurement data remains fragmented across contracting authorities, platforms and financial systems, limiting the ability of public authorities to aggregate demand, compare prices, assess supplier performance and identify emerging risks. 1.
Does the Commission consider procurement and expenditure data to be a strategic public-sector asset for improving public financial management and administrative capacity?
Will the Commission assess whether fragmented procurement data limits Member States’ ability to benchmark costs, aggregate demand, manage suppliers and secure value for money?
In the context of the future public procurement act, will the Commission consider measures to help Member States develop more interoperable procurement data systems?
